missing_methods.detailed_requirements: This method should verify that the edit feedback screen is displayed after clicking the feedback button. It should check for the presence of key elements such as the feedback slide title, the tell your experience text field, and the submit button. The method should wait for these elements to be visible and return True if the screen is successfully opened, otherwise raise an exception or return False. This verification ensures the user has successfully navigated to the feedback input screen.
implementation_checklist: Wait for 'hpx_feedback_page_title' to be visible using self.driver.wait_for_object
Wait for 'tell_your_experience_title' to be visible using self.driver.wait_for_object
Swipe to 'edit_feedback' using self.driver.swipe
Wait for 'edit_feedback' to be visible using self.driver.wait_for_object
Swipe to 'send_feedback_submit_btn' using self.driver.swipe
Wait for 'send_feedback_submit_btn' to be visible using self.driver.wait_for_object
Return True if all elements are successfully found, otherwise raise exception or return False

missing_methods.detailed_requirements: This method should locate the 'tell your experience' text input field (edit_feedback element) and input the provided text string. The method should first wait for the text field to be visible and enabled, clear any existing text if necessary, then send the provided text to the field. It should handle scrolling to the element if needed. The method should accept a text parameter and return None or a confirmation of successful input.
implementation_checklist: Swipe to 'edit_feedback' using self.driver.swipe to ensure element is in view
Wait for 'edit_feedback' to be visible using self.driver.wait_for_object
Click 'edit_feedback' to focus the text field using self.driver.click
Clear existing text in 'edit_feedback' if necessary (check if element has existing value)
Send keys to 'edit_feedback' using self.driver.send_keys with the provided text parameter
Return None or confirmation of successful input

missing_methods.intent: Assert tell your experience text is truncated
missing_methods.detailed_requirements: This method should verify that the text entered in the 'tell your experience' field is truncated to a maximum character limit. It should retrieve the current text value from the feedback text field using get_entered_text() or by directly accessing the element's value attribute. The method should compare the length of the entered text against the expected maximum length (e.g., 1000 characters based on the character count feature). It should assert that the text length does not exceed the maximum allowed length and optionally verify that the character count display shows the correct truncated count. The method should raise an assertion error if the text is not properly truncated.
implementation_checklist: Swipe to 'edit_feedback' using self.driver.swipe to ensure element is in view
Wait for 'edit_feedback' to be visible using self.driver.wait_for_object
Call existing get_entered_text() method to retrieve current text value from 'edit_feedback'
Calculate the length of the retrieved text using len()
Assert that the text length does not exceed expected_max_length parameter
Wait for 'edit_feedback_char_count' to be visible using self.driver.wait_for_object
Get the character count display text from 'edit_feedback_char_count' using self.driver.get_attribute with 'Name' attribute
Parse the character count display text to extract current count and max count
Assert that the current count matches the length of retrieved text and does not exceed expected_max_length
Raise AssertionError with descriptive message if text is not properly truncated
